utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. Mr. Trbic, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we have the first problem of the day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: My English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He should have it in, I don't know what channel, Serbo-Croat channel. I'll repeat what I said again. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much Mr. Trbic. And good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Peter McCloskey with Lada Soljan and Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you and your team. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Stephane Piletta-Zanin for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, the second problem. I am hearing interpretation in English but also in Serbo-Croat, one after the other. That would double the length of the proceedings. So this is the first time we come face to face, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please allow me to extend to you a very warm, warm welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can only thank you for your greetings, all the more so since it is very likely that it's going to be for a very short time. I thank you nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Perhaps you can explain that in due course. Not simply for formalities' sake but also for the record, may I just point out that this is the first status conference that is being held following the decision on severance. It is within the 120-day limit prescribed by Rule 65 bis. The purpose of status conferences is twofold. Basically, even more than that, namely to organise exchanges between the parties with a view to ensuring an expeditious preparation for trial, and secondly, to allow the accused to raise issues in relation to his mental and physical condition. Some days ago, or a couple of weeks ago, I gave instructions to Senior Legal Officer of Trial Chamber II to convene a 65 ter meeting between the parties with a view to preparing the agenda for this status conference. I will go straight to the first item on the agenda and that is outstanding motions. There are as such no outstanding motions pending before this Tribunal -- sorry, before this Trial Chamber, but there is a major motion pending before the 11 bis Referral Bench. This was filed on the 4th of May 2006 by the Prosecution. And on the 10th of May, it was referred to the Referral Bench, the motion is still pending before that Bench for reasons that I suppose are -- not I suppose, I'm sure you're both aware of. There is also of course pending before the Appeals Chamber the appeal that was filed by the accused following our decision on severance. That -- those proceedings, he's contesting the decision of Trial Chamber II, and I will -- unless I hear any comments arising of that, but I don't imagine there would be any, I move to the second item on the agenda, which deals with disclosure matters, and as you know, usually deal under this heading or deal with this subject under two separate headings, one disclosure under Rule 66(A)(i) and (A)(ii) and the other under Rule 68. I'll go straight to the point. I know this was discussed thoroughly yesterday during the 65 ter meeting and the report I got back from the Senior Legal Officer is clear but not clear enough. In other words, there seems to be something that needed more or something that would require more information. I'm informed that yesterday, he was not really put in a position where he could report to me that disclosure under Rule 66(A)(i) and Rule 66(A)(ii) had been completed. It's not that it has not been completed but we still require to know whether it has been completed. Neither you nor the Defence could provide Mr. Cubbon with a straightforward, 100 per cent correct answer. So if you can -- I'll go back on this subject and I will ask Prosecution first to maybe enlighten us on the position now. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's my understanding, Mr. President, that 66(A)(i) was completed 29 June, 2005 and 66(A)(ii) is practically completed but it's a bit of an ongoing process as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And do you have a date in sight when you would think that you would complete disclosure under this second provision?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As the case that we -- that we are aware of now, I can't think of any more witnesses but there may be witnesses of a health nature or things like that that may come up, but as far as I know, we've finished it for the time being until we get perhaps a little more clarity on where we are going with the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In this respect I'd like to make two observations. Firstly, as I pointed out yesterday, in the light of the urgency as I was assigned counsel in this case, I was not able to check point by point whether the case file I was given in a very excellent way by the previous counsel of Mr. Trbic matches in all points the disclosure made by the Prosecution. I think it would have been useless for me to do that. My premise was that the dossier, the file was okay. Secondly there is a more fundamental problem. There are for instance some medical expert reports, the latest one being of the 28th of August 2006, and initially, they had been done in Croatian, I believe, apparently these expert reports were only conveyed to my client yesterday, so that -- and I saw him yesterday. I was not able to discuss this thoroughly with him and the purpose of disclosure is, after all, in my view, to enable the accused to know what it is all about. So there is a basic problem here on the merits because it is in my view inadmissible that the administration, which at a stage of it is concerned, discloses such evidence only a few minutes before a client meets his lawyer and a few hours before such a hearing as this. This is in my view inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One point that I want to follow up from what you've just stated, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You said there are for instance some medical expert reports, the latest one being of the 28th of August of this year, and initially they had been done in Croatian. Did I have the correct interpretation or is there something wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes indeed. Your interpretation was right because these reports were drafted initially in Croatian, in the Croatian language. What I mean by this, Your Honour, is that we don't even have the excuse of translation from English into B/C/S, because initially -- originally, the reports were written in B/C/S or, rather, in Croatian to be more exact. So I fail to understand why this would be such a delay. Was I clear enough this time? I know -- I used not to be, you know. I never am clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I know what you're saying. These are probably the reports, medical reports, that have not yet been handed over by the detention unit authorities and then they were handed over. Are these the reports? Or are you referring to the report of the psychiatrist appointed by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely I have in mind those two reports which are basically only one. I think they are dated the 28th of August 2006. I'm not quite sure but I believe it is the date and they were originally drafted in B/C/S and they were physically handed over to my client only on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any comments on that, Mr. McCloskey? What was the nationality of the psychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we received her report in a very expedited fashion on the 31st of August. We filed it with the Registry September 1st. They should have sent it as they normally do electronically to Defence counsel. It's shortly thereafter. We don't, as you know, provide material such as this directly to the accused. That would be inappropriate. We have asked for it to be translated into English. This is the situation where we have the language of the accused so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know because to my knowledge there isn't much difference between Serbian and Croat, I've had a full two hour explanation about the difference between the two languages in the past so I know a little bit about it, but any way, let's cut this short. This is fundamental. It's a right that the accused has. What I'm going to do is I am going to establish time limit, fix a time limit, of two weeks from now during which you do a little bit your homework to find out whether there are any further -- there is any further material that needs to be disclosed under 65(A)(ii). You will by the end of this two-week period file a declaration stating what your conclusion is or what your findings are, and then I'll establish a further date by which you will be needed to complete your disclosure. Is two weeks sufficient for you, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I've been able to focus a little more on this situation in the last night and this morning, I can tell you now, as far as we know, we have -- I don't have at this point any more witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Or statements to provide. As you can see, it says copies of all written statements taken in accordance with 92 bis, and we plan to follow up with this accused just like we will follow up in the other case and we now have our marching orders on that, so we will continue to follow. So we are following the previous order. We are treating this accused as we are with the others. So we are up to date as far as we know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I take it that except for the material related to the issue, the only issue that is still pending before this Trial Chamber for the time being, rest has been disclosed already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm confident we are in good shape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the rest will be an ongoing process as we proceed along the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing. Thank you, Your Honour. You tell the Prosecution to do their homework very well. In that respect, could they not check one thing, in the interest of Mr. Trbic, that this whole disclosure process be efficient, in other words, that they make sure that documents be disclosed in Serbian or Croatian because otherwise it's not of any use to our client. OLAD denied me the right of having a series of potential co-counsel so that I do not have any full time assistant in my team, unlike the Prosecution team, my team doesn't have anybody who is conversant in Serbian or Croatian so this had better be checked in the interest of the accused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Prosecution knows exactly which documents are required by law to disclose in the language of the accused. If there are any shortcomings in that respect, you will of course attract the wrath of the Trial Chamber. So please do it and to that make sure that what has been disclosed has been disclosed according to the law. Not everything needs according to our Rules to be disclosed in the language of the accused. The other type of disclosure relates to Rule 68. I take it from what has been reported to me by Mr. Cubbon that you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, confirmed having received a CD from the Prosecution purportedly to contain Rule 68 exculpatory material. I just want to confirm whether there is anything else the Prosecution would like to add in respect to this type of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We are up to date, and as you said, we are being assisted in our obligations by seven other Defence counsel that are keeping us on our toes, and I could -- it would be of great assistance in meeting our Rule 68 obligation if Mr. Trbic has anything in particular that he views as exculpatory or even generally to tell us. That way we can do the searching and we can get material like that to him as we have stated to all the other accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. There is one further matter that I would like to raise before we go into more delicate matters, and that is following a decision that we -- when I say we, it's Trial Chamber II, in sitting -- in presiding over the Popovic case. Upon the severance, we had also ordered that a new indictment be drawn up in respect to Mr. Trbic. What I want to confirm is that the indictment that I have received, at least in English, has been translated and provided and forwarded to the accused. In other words, whether he has received the indictment now in his own language. Perhaps -- I don't know whether you are in a position to confirm that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm that I did not receive it in French, Your Honour, but that's not the question you put. I will confess that we did not look into this question yesterday, Mr. Trbic and I, but I believe that in the meeting, in the 65 ter meeting, it appeared that either it was being served or Mr. Trbic had just received it and he would say otherwise if it were the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Trbic, I just want a statement from you in case you have not received the indictment, the new indictment, in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I did receive the indictment yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I thank you for that. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we've come to the end of this status conference. We had to dedicate part of it or deal part of it in private session because of particular reasons that required us to be in private session. There being no further issues to address, I declare this Status Conference closed here. We adjourn and I also wish to thank you, Mr. McCloskey, Ms. Soljan and you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for your cooperation and your courtesy. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
